hints: Recall the classic halide test with silver nitrate, the precipitate colours get darker going down Group 17.
Place the three colours in order: $\text{AgCl}$ is white, so $\text{AgBr}$ must be the middle cream colour and $\text{AgI}$ the darkest yellow.
Think about which precipitate dissolves most easily, $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in dilute ammonia while $\text{AgBr}$ needs concentrated ammonia and $\text{AgI}$ stays insoluble.
walkthrough:
**Recall the precipitate colours**

This is the standard test for halide ions with $\text{AgNO}_3(aq)$. The colours darken down the group as the halide ion gets larger and more polarisable.

$$\text{AgCl: white} \rightarrow \text{AgBr: cream} \rightarrow \text{AgI: yellow}$$

**Identify the colour of AgBr**

$\text{AgBr}$ is in the middle, so it is cream. It is darker than white $\text{AgCl}$ but paler than yellow $\text{AgI}$.

**Compare solubility in aqueous ammonia**

Ammonia dissolves the precipitates by forming the complex $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$. The least stable lattice dissolves most easily.

$$\text{AgCl soluble in dilute NH}_3(aq) > \text{AgBr soluble in concentrated NH}_3(aq) > \text{AgI insoluble}$$

**Pick the correct row**

Cream colour for $\text{AgBr}$ plus most soluble halide as $\text{AgCl}$ gives the only fully correct combination.

options.A: Correct. AgBr is cream (between white AgCl and yellow AgI) and AgCl is most soluble in NH3(aq) as it dissolves even in dilute ammonia.
options.B: Wrong on solubility. The colour cream for AgBr is right, but AgI is insoluble in ammonia, not the most soluble. Students sometimes reverse the solubility trend.
options.C: Wrong on colour. AgCl is the most soluble, which is correct, but AgBr is cream not yellow. Yellow is the colour of AgI, the darkest precipitate.
options.D: Wrong on both. Yellow is AgI not AgBr, and AgI is insoluble in NH3(aq). This swaps both the colour trend and the solubility trend.
